sections.headline: Three concrete checks *for an existing Wix site.*
sections.lede: Prepared in response to a public request for technical SEO work. This is an independent review of the pages anyone can load. It is not a client engagement, a Search Console inspection or a claim about rankings.

items.title: Search intent is diluted
items.text: The delivered title leads with “elite accreditation services review”, and the page has a second primary heading phrased as a review. A service buyer is more directly served by a title such as “Healthcare Accreditation Consultants | Elite Accreditation” and a service-led introduction.

items.title: The same long introduction repeats
items.text: Several testimonial blocks carry the same broad service-description paragraphs. Make each testimonial concise, keep one authoritative service introduction, and link to the specific service pages instead of repeating the same text.

items.title: The HTML response is 2,320,224 bytes
items.text: That is the uncompressed response-body size observed in this run, not a Core Web Vitals score. Inspect Wix apps, video embeds and repeated sections, then measure mobile loading before and after each change.

sections.title: What was inspected
sections.caveat: A reachable sitemap is not proof of Google indexing. “Discovered, not indexed” and “Crawled, not indexed” need their actual URL examples and Search Console evidence before assigning a cause.

sections.title: A first implementation pass — without a platform migration

items.title: Baseline
items.text: Record current Wix settings and selected service pages, then inspect Search Console examples with owner-approved read access.

items.title: Correct high-intent pages
items.text: Refine homepage and key ASC/DME service titles, headings and internal links, preserving the site and its existing content ownership.

items.title: Measure the change
items.text: Recheck rendered pages and crawlability; track indexing and qualified enquiries separately. No paid backlinks or ranking guarantees.

pages.title: A training app for a studio

sections.headline: One training app. *Every studio its own.*
sections.lede: A sample built for a strength studio and a yoga studio. Members train from their phone, coaches write and publish the programmes, and each studio keeps its own name, colours and typeface. The studios and members shown here are made up.

items.title: Open today’s session
items.text: The day’s workout is on the first screen, with the week around it and what was done last time.

picture.alt: The Today screen of a studio training app showing the next session

items.title: Pick a programme
items.text: Members choose from the programmes the studio has published and add one to their own plan.

picture.alt: A list of published training programmes

items.title: Log each set
items.text: A timer, the next exercise and a rest prompt. Sets are saved on the phone, so a session carries on in a basement gym with no signal.

picture.alt: A workout in progress with a timer and the next set

items.title: Answer requests
items.text: A member asks for a programme. The coach picks the request up, drafts a plan and sends it back to that member.

picture.alt: A coach’s list of programme requests from members

items.title: Publish programmes
items.text: A programme is reviewed before it goes out. Each change is a new version, and a programme can be withdrawn.

picture.alt: A coach’s list of programmes with their published versions

items.title: Set the studio’s look
items.text: Name, colours, typeface and mark are set in one place and the member app follows.

picture.alt: The appearance settings for a studio, with colour and typeface choices

items.title: Review a workout from your watch
items.text: Choose a TCX workout file from an app that supports export. Review its duration, distance and heart rate before adding it to your history. Apple Watch and Wear OS exports use the same review.

items.title: Put your plan on your calendar
items.text: Share upcoming sessions with a calendar app or download the calendar file, even offline. Each session is an all-day event. Calendar copies do not update when your plan changes.

items.title: Connect a heart-rate sensor
items.text: Pair a compatible Bluetooth heart-rate sensor in a supported browser and choose whether to save readings with your workout. Physical-device checks are still pending. Direct Apple Health and Health Connect sync and watch controls are not available yet.

sections.title: What is in the sample, and what is not

items.title: Working now
items.text: Programmes, sessions and history on the member’s own device, offline use, heart-rate sensors, workout files from a watch, calendar export, coach requests and versioned publishing. A studio can also let an assistant read its published programmes, read-only.

items.title: Not in the sample
items.text: Paid memberships and card payments. Those would be agreed and built for your studio and your payment provider.

items.title: See it running
items.text: The app runs on your own server, so there is no public copy to click through. Ask for a walk-through on a call.
